fuentes: National Weather Service, Cold / Polar Vortex (weather.gov/safety/cold-polar-vortex): 'a large area of low pressure and cold air surrounding both of the Earth's poles'; always exists near the poles, weakens in summer and strengthens in winter; polar vortexes are not something new; the vortex will expand, sending cold air southward with the jet stream; often associated with large outbreaks of Arctic air in the United States; the only danger to humans is how cold temperatures get; check forecast on weather.gov; check home and car emergency kits at the beginning of each winter season
NOAA Climate.gov, Understanding the Arctic polar vortex

frases.texto: The "polar vortex" on the news isn't a storm coming for your town.
It's a huge area of cold air circling each pole, all year.
In winter it strengthens, and it helps keep the coldest air up north.
When it expands, cold air can get sent south on the jet stream.
The National Weather Service says that's often tied to Arctic air outbreaks in the U.S.
Heads up: it's nothing new, and the real danger is just how cold it gets.
Check your forecast at weather.gov, and check your car's emergency kit each winter.
So what's the coldest it's ever gotten where you live?
Send this to the friend who says "polar vortex" when it's just chilly.
